what: PU Verificado — pre-registration, written 2026-10-16 before any price was decided at scale (a scout had reproduced 3 ANBIMA LTN rows and 5 of 6 Tesouro Direto rows by hand on 2026-10-16; nothing else was looked at). Phase A: the fixed-rate titles of Tesouro Direto.
claim: Every published Tesouro Direto unit price (PU) of a fixed-rate title is the value its own methodology gives for the published rate, the official holiday calendar and the rule table — digit for digit at the precision the publisher prints.

scope.source: corpus/pu/sources/precotaxatesourodireto.csv (sha256 in PINS.json), every row whose Tipo Titulo is 'Tesouro Prefixado' (LTN) or 'Tesouro Prefixado com Juros Semestrais' (NTN-F), both sides (compra, venda) and the base PU, 2004-12-31 to the file's last day
scope.outOfScope: Tesouro Selic (LFT), IPCA+ (NTN-B / NTN-B Principal), IGPM+ (NTN-C), Educa+, Renda+ — phase B (they need VNA and the pro-rata projection, which carries a NEEDS DATA where the projection used is not recorded); ANBIMA's secondary-market file (republication terms unsettled); B3's prices
scope.calendar: corpus/pu/holidays.json read from the pinned ANBIMA feriados_nacionais.xls; weekends are not business days; du = business days from the settlement date (inclusive) to the payment date (exclusive), as the STN methodology defines

rules.source: STN, Metodologia de Cálculo dos Títulos Públicos Federais Ofertados nos Leilões Primários, 29/04/2024, Tabela 3 'Regras para o Cálculo Preciso' (= ANBIMA Metodologias de Precificação 2021 §22). A = round, T = truncate, at the stated decimals.
rules.LTN: PU = 1000 / (1 + taxa)^(du/252); taxa in % a.a. T-6; the exponent du/252 T-14; PU T-6
rules.NTN-F: coupon = 1000 × ((1.10)^(1/2) − 1) A-5 (= 48.80885); each discounted flow coupon_k / (1 + taxa)^(du_k/252 T-14) A-9, the last flow carrying 1000 + coupon; PU = Σ flows T-6; coupons on 1 January and 1 July, the last at maturity
rules.printed: the CSV prints PU at 2 decimals (R$ and centavos). The rule table's 'Valor Financeiro T-2' is the only 2-decimal rule it states. Two readings are pre-registered and both are recorded per row: TRUNC-2 (the printed PU equals the T-6 PU truncated at 2 decimals) and ROUND-2 (equals it rounded at 2 decimals). Which reading each publisher side follows, by year, is a CENSUS the record reports; the verdict REPRODUCED needs one of the two readings to hold and the record says which.
rules.settlement: the CSV's 'Data Base' is the quotation day. Settlement hypotheses pre-registered: for the buy side D+1 (the next business day) and D+0; for the sell side D+0 and D+1. Each row is decided under both and the record keeps both; the CENSUS says which hypothesis reproduces each side in each year. A row that reproduces under neither is OFF.

verdicts.REPRODUCED: the T-6 PU is decided (the enclosure does not straddle the truncation boundary) and the printed 2-decimal PU equals its TRUNC-2 or its ROUND-2 under one of the pre-registered settlement hypotheses; the record says which reading and which hypothesis
verdicts.OFF: the T-6 PU is decided and the printed PU equals neither reading under any pre-registered hypothesis; the record carries the exact T-6 value, the printed value, the difference in centavos, and the nearest hypothesis
verdicts.REFUSED: the enclosure of the T-6 PU straddles a truncation boundary at the precision computed (the decision would need a wider enclosure); the row is not claimed either way
verdicts.NEEDS DATA: an input the decision needs is not in the pinned sources (phase A expects none for LTN/NTN-F; reserved for phase B's projections)

arithmetic: exact rationals for every step the rule defines; the one irrational step (1 + taxa)^(exponent) as an enclosure — JavaScript BigInt fixed point with explicit series remainders (instruments/pu/decide.js) and, sharing no code, Python decimal at 60 digits with directed rounding around correctly rounded ln/exp (instruments/pu/decide.py); the two must agree on every decided digit on the cross-checked sample or the run refuses
calibration: before any CSV row is decided, both deciders must reproduce the methodology's own worked examples: LTN taxa 14.3600, du 532 → 753.315323; the NTN-F example in the same document; and a planted holiday must change du by one
redControls: a planted extra holiday on a settlement date must move du by one and turn a REPRODUCED row OFF
rounding the exponent instead of truncating it (A-14 for T-14) must turn at least one row OFF or REFUSED on the sample
rounding the PU at 6 decimals instead of truncating must turn at least one row OFF on the sample
a shifted settlement (D+2) must turn the buy-side census away from REPRODUCED
a corrupted CSV byte must refuse the run (the pin)
the two deciders disagreeing on one digit must refuse the run
whatCountsAsAResult: the census of conventions per side and year; the count of REPRODUCED / OFF / REFUSED rows per title and year; every OFF row with its exact value and difference; every REFUSED row with its enclosure. All green is a result and gets the same page. A difference is a 'slip' in the publisher's number as printed, never a refutation of the publisher's methodology, and is stated as such.
notClaimed: that any publisher erred — a convention the publisher used and did not publish (a calendar, a settlement rule, a rounding of the rate before truncation) is a NEEDS DATA reading, named; that the ANBIMA or B3 prices agree or disagree (phase B)

amendments.after: the first 4,000 rows (the most recent, 2026 → late 2025) were decided; 7,979 of 8,000 (row, side) pairs REPRODUCED, 21 OFF
amendments.seen: all 21 OFF are buy-side rows quoted on 2025-12-23 and 2025-12-30. The printed prices are HIGHER than the D+1 value by 23–55 centavos on the LTNs, and LOWER by one coupon (≈ R$ 48.3) on the NTN-Fs quoted 2025-12-30 — the signature of a settlement on 2025-12-26 and 2026-01-02: the business days 24 December and 31 December skipped, and the 1 January coupon gone ex. The pinned ANBIMA calendar says in its own notes that it does not list the last business day of the year (Resolução 2.596/99) and lists only days that close bank reserves; 24 December is a B3 half-day without settlement.
amendments.change: a third settlement hypothesis is added for the buy side, D+1x = the next business day that is neither 24 December nor 31 December, and recorded per row like the others. The PRIMARY hypothesis stays D+1 as pre-registered; a row that reproduces only under D+1x is classed REPRODUCED with the code D1x and counted apart in the census, so the reader sees how many prices need the unlisted non-settlement days. This is a convention the publisher follows and the pinned calendar documents only by omission; it is named, not assumed.
amendments.notChanged: the readings (TRUNC-2, ROUND-2), the sell-side hypotheses, the verdict definitions, the rule table

amendments.after: the full run of 55,588 rows (111,101 (row, side) pairs): 92,265 REPRODUCED, 18,798 OFF, 38 NEEDS DATA (settlement on or after maturity). The OFF rows are 2014–2023 quotations of titles maturing 2025 and later, spread over every month and weekday, both sides.
amendments.seen: on a seeded sample of 30 OFF LTN rows, the printed price is reproduced exactly when du is increased by 1 for maturity 2025-01-01, by 2 for 2026-01-01 and by 4 for 2029-01-01 — the number of weekday 20 Novembers between settlement and maturity (20 Nov 2027 is a Saturday). 20 November became a national holiday by Lei 14.759 of 21 December 2023; the pinned ANBIMA file lists it from 2024 on. The publisher priced each quotation with the calendar in force on the day of the quotation, in which no future 20 November was a holiday; the file pinned today carries them, so today's calendar re-counts every earlier quotation.
amendments.change: a second calendar hypothesis is added: CALENDAR-AS-OF-QUOTE, the pinned list minus the 20 Novembers of 2024 and later for quotations before the publisher adopted the new holiday. Every pair is decided under today's calendar and under the as-of-quote calendar; a row that reproduces only under the as-of-quote calendar is REPRODUCED with the code suffix /pre and counted apart. The adoption date is NOT assumed: it is read from the census as the first quotation date from which today's calendar reproduces and the as-of-quote one does not.
amendments.notChanged: the readings, the settlement hypotheses (D+0, D+1, D+1x), the verdict definitions, the rule table. The primary hypothesis for an OFF row's reported difference stays today's calendar, D+1 buy / D+0 sell.

amendments.after: the phase-A ledger (887 OFF) and the phase-B data scout
amendments.seen: the OFF rows cluster on quotation days whose next bank business day is a day B3 did not trade: 25 January and 9 July through 2021, 20 November 2006–2021 (not 2020), 24 and 31 December (the Friday before when 31 December is a weekend), the 2014 World Cup days, and 2 January 2018 (the Treasury asked for the first settlement of 2018 on the second business day, OC 111/2016). B3's own circulars (2017–2026) and Wayback captures of the exchange's calendar pages (2004–2016) state the rules; the 2007, 2008 and 2014-July pages were not found.
amendments.change: B1 as pre-registered in phaseB: tools/pu-b3-calendar.js derives corpus/pu/b3-settlement.json from the pinned documents — seven rules, each date citing the documents covering its year that name the holiday; a date no document names is RULE-ONLY and a settlement path through it is coded /r and counted apart. Hypotheses D1b3 (buy) and D0b3, D1b3 (sell): settlement on the next day B3 traded. The July 2014 match days are NOT in the table (no document captured): those rows stay OFF. QuantLib's Brazil::Exchange is the cross-check, not the authority.
amendments.notChanged: everything else; the primary hypothesis for an OFF row's reported difference stays D+1 buy / D+0 sell on today's bank calendar

amendments.after: the LFT deciders were written against the methodology's worked example, before any LFT row of the CSV was decided
amendments.seen: the example (maturity 07/03/2014, settlement 21/05/2008, taxa −0,0200%, Meta Selic 11,75%) reproduces only if the projection factor (1 + meta)^(trunc14(1/252)) multiplies the VNA at full precision — truncating that factor at 4, 6 or 8 decimals gives a different VNA projetado; the accumulated Selic factor rounded at 16 decimals at each daily step and rounded once at the end both give the printed VNA 3.449,694215.
amendments.change: B2 reads the projection factor as an enclosure at full precision (the result truncated at 6, as the table says for VNA projetado), and the accumulated factor as A-16 at each step (the primary; the once-at-the-end reading is recorded where the two differ at the printed digits). SGS 432 (the Selic target) is pinned beside SGS 11 as the meta input. For the sell side at D+0 the VNA of the quotation day is the exact index; for any settlement after the quotation the projected VNA from the meta of the quotation day.
amendments.notChanged: the verdicts, the settlement and calendar hypotheses, the reading of the printed centavos

amendments.after: the first run with the LFT rows (77,053 rows) — 13,026 OFF or REFUSED, almost all LFT; then a probe of 400 LFT buy-side rows from 2020 on under the primary hypothesis
amendments.seen: (a) a zero rate (0,00 — common for the LFT) was REFUSED by the enclosure's outward slack although (1 + 0)^E is exactly 1: fixed, the power of a zero rate is exact. (b) Of 400 recent LFT rows, 14 reproduce exactly, 386 lie inside the interval of prices the printed rate's own precision allows (rate ± half a unit of its last printed decimal) and 0 lie outside: Tesouro Direto prints the LFT ágio/deságio at 2 decimals and prices with more. The early years (2006–2019 in the probe) reproduce exactly.
amendments.change: the verdict CONSISTENT (the grammar of the return-levels paper) is added: a row not REPRODUCED under any hypothesis whose printed centavos lie within [trunc2(PU(rate − ½ unit)), round2(PU(rate + ½ unit))] under the primary hypothesis. It is counted apart from REPRODUCED and from OFF, for every title; a row outside that interval stays OFF. It states what the published rate's precision allows and nothing more.

amendments.after: the full run of 77,053 rows (145,439 prices): 966 OFF, of which 746 LFT and, of those, 527 sell-side rows quoted May 2020 – November 2021 that neither settlement reproduced (typical difference 80–290 centavos). A probe of the implied rate behind every printed Tesouro Selic price of 2019–2022 (float, a probe, not a decision) under D+0 and D+1.
amendments.seen: the LFT sell side settled D+1 until September 2021 and D+0 from October 2021 — the same switch the ledger’s own sellSwitch census already records for the fixed-rate titles (last D+1-only day 2021-09-10). Under D+1 the printed sell price of 737 of 747 LFT rows of 2020 and 704 of 977 of 2021 lies inside the interval the printed rate’s half-unit allows; under D+0 only 345 and 646 do. The verdict CONSISTENT (amendment 5) was decided under the PRIMARY hypothesis alone (D+0 for the sell side), so a row whose period settled D+1 could never be CONSISTENT and fell to OFF although the same box, under the settlement the census shows for its period, contains the printed centavos. The buy side shows the same under D+1 (its primary), so it was unaffected. Rows the box contains under NEITHER settlement: 10 and 28 (sell), 9 and 29 (buy) in 2020 and 2021; among them the November–December 2021 and 2022 sell rows whose implied rate sits 0.0051–0.0053 above the printed one — just past the half-unit, as a rate truncated (not rounded) to two decimals would sit. No document pinned here says the rate is truncated; those rows stay OFF and are named. The 2025-12-30 buy rows (9) sit inside the box under the B3 settlement (2026-01-02) and outside it under the primary.
amendments.change: CONSISTENT is decided under every settlement hypothesis the row was decided under (the same set REPRODUCED uses: D+0, D+1, D+1x, the B3 settlements, each on today’s calendar and the as-of-quote one), the primary tried first; the record keeps `under` (the first hypothesis that holds) and `codes` (every one), and the ledger counts CONSISTENT rows by code and by side and year under each hypothesis. The verdict word, the box (rate ± half a unit of the last printed decimal), the readings and the primary hypothesis for an OFF row’s reported difference are unchanged. What the amendment adds is symmetry: REPRODUCED already accepted any pre-registered settlement; CONSISTENT now does too.
amendments.notChanged: the rule table, the readings, the settlement and calendar hypotheses, the verdict definitions of REPRODUCED, OFF, REFUSED and NEEDS DATA; no hypothesis about a truncated rate is added — an undocumented convention stays OFF and named
amendments.result: RECORDED AFTER THE RUN (2026-10-16, late night; the fields above were written before it): 145,439 prices — 132,362 REPRODUCED (unchanged), 12,779 CONSISTENT (from 12,050), 237 OFF (from 966; LFT 746 → 44, every one of them 2008–2018), 0 REFUSED, 61 NEEDS DATA. Of the CONSISTENT rows, 12,652 hold under the side’s primary settlement and 127 only under another (D+1x 28, B3 25, the as-of-quote calendar 74: D1/pre 27, D0/pre 47) — but the bySideYearUnder census shows the sell side of 2020–2021 CONSISTENT under D+1 for 515 rows, which the primary D+0 had placed OFF. The November–December 2021 and 2022 sell rows the probe put 0.0051–0.0053 past the half-unit are CONSISTENT under D+0 on the calendar in force on the quotation day (D0/pre): the probe had counted business days on today’s calendar, which carries three 20 Novembers those quotations could not know. No truncation signature remains; the suspicion recorded above is withdrawn by the record. The 2025-12-30 buy rows are CONSISTENT under D+1x (9). The Python decider re-derived all 237 OFF rows and a seeded sample (1,737/1,737 agree).

phaseB.registered: 2026-10-16 (evening), before any phase-B row was decided
phaseB.B1_settlementCalendar: Hypothesis: Tesouro Direto settles on B3's trading calendar, not on the national bank calendar the methodology counts du on; the 887 OFF rows of phase A are quotations whose next business day is a day B3 did not settle (25 January, 9 July, 20 November in the years B3 observed them; 24 and 31 December). The calendar will be PINNED FROM B3'S OWN PUBLICATION (or QuantLib's documented Brazil exchange rules as a cross-check), never inferred from the price data; a row that reproduces only under it gets the code suffix /b3 and is counted apart. The number of OFF rows that remain after it is the result.
phaseB.B2_LFT: Tesouro Selic: PU = cotação (T-4) × VNA; VNA = 1000 × the accumulated daily Selic factor from 2000-07-01 (fator acumulado A-16, VNA T-6) from BCB SGS series 11 pinned; the cotação from the published rate with du to maturity. Verdicts as phase A. If the publisher's VNA is published, both the recomputed and the published VNA are decided; a VNA that cannot be recomputed from pinned Selic is NEEDS DATA.
phaseB.B3_NTNB: Tesouro IPCA+: VNA by IPCA from SIDRA 1737 pinned, with the pro-rata projection between the 15th and the next index release. The projection the publisher used on each historical day is expected NOT to be public: those rows are NEEDS DATA by construction and the count of them is the headline of that slice. Rows after the month's IPCA is known are decided with the realised index only where the methodology says the realised index applies.
phaseB.B4_feed: tools/pu-feed.js + .github/workflows/pu-feed.yml: the published CSV is admitted only if every pinned row is present byte for byte and new rows carry later dates; a restatement refuses the day and is logged (corpus/pu/feed-log.json) — a publisher rewriting history is a finding. The pin chain is kept in PINS.json history. The ledger is re-decided whole at every admitted day.
phaseB.B5_instrument: /instruments/pu: the same decide.js bytes in the browser; a rate, a settlement date and a maturity give the T-6 price with its enclosure and every truncation step; pasted Tesouro Direto rows are decided to the verdicts of the ledger. The page states no number of its own.
phaseB.notDoing: ANBIMA's secondary-market prices until republication terms are settled; B3's own prices; any claim about why a publisher chose a convention.
